extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and administrators at Canadian postsecondary institutions seeking SSHRC funding
extracted.subtask_description: An agency-level overview of SSHRC funding types, basic eligibility signals, and links to application, review, policy, and support resources for social sciences and humanities researchers and students in Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant is an amount of money given by a government to a person or organization for a special purpose. SSHRC offers a wide range of grants to researchers, including joint initiatives in partnership with other organizations, that have either open or targeted themes, as well as grants for research-creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Find grants' to discover specific grant programs and their requirements (themes may be open or targeted; some grants support research-creation or joint initiatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: A scholarship is a form of financial aid awarded to students for further education. SSHRC awards scholarships to students enrolled in, or who have applied for or will apply for full-time admission to a graduate program in the social sciences and humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility centers on student status and full-time graduate program admission; consult specific scholarship pages for deadlines and application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship may take the form of financial support, an academic position, a training program or a combination of these. At SSHRC, a number of fellowships are offered to support promising researchers who have completed an eligible doctoral degree (PhD) or PhD-equivalent program of study in the social sciences and humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship eligibility is oriented to those with an eligible doctoral degree or equivalent; program formats and expectations vary by fellowship—see individual fellowship descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and prizes (Impact Awards & Storytellers Challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC celebrates achievements with the SSHRC Impact Awards (candidates are nominated by eligible Canadian postsecondary institutions). The Storytellers Challenge invites undergraduate and graduate students to compete for prizes by creating short videos or presentations showing how social sciences and humanities research is affecting our lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact Awards rely on institutional nominations; Storytellers Challenge submissions should be concise media/presentations demonstrating research impact—see each program for submission rules and judging criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental funding or training opportunities, generally offered by external organizations, are available through some SSHRC and tri-agency funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement availability, eligibility, and conditions are specified in each funding opportunity description—applicants must read the specific funding opportunity to learn more.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to apply (application components and eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on subject matter eligibility, application instructions, how to use the Canadian Common CV, definitions of terms, and the SSHRC lexicon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the 'How to apply' resources for detailed application instructions, CV formatting (Canadian Common CV), and definitions that affect eligibility and completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: How applications are reviewed (merit review process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the merit review process at SSHRC, including review principles, reviewer roles, review committees, review of Indigenous research, and how to get involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review follows defined principles and committee roles; applicants should review these materials to understand assessment weightings, Indigenous research review practices, and opportunities to serve or participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms and online application tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Help with online forms, direct deposit, progress report forms, consent to disclosure forms, and discipline codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tools and forms to complete submissions and post-award reporting; ensure correct discipline codes and completed consent/disclosure documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies, regulations and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC, tri-agency and Government of Canada policies and guidelines pertaining to all aspects of the research funding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees must follow applicable SSHRC/tri-agency/Government of Canada policies—consult the relevant policy pages for eligibility rules, research integrity, and administration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: The journey of a SSHRC application
rubrics_metrics.description: An overview of how applications are processed and adjudicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides applicants with expectations about timelines, stages of adjudication, and procedural steps from submission to decision and award management.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSHRC terminology (lexicon and definitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of terms and a lexicon of terminology used by SSHRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the SSHRC lexicon to interpret program language, eligibility requirements, and application instructions consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Your Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about safeguarding your research against theft, interference, or unwanted transfer of knowledge and results in ways that individuals and teams do not intend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should consider research security risks and mitigation strategies when planning projects and collaborations; follow SSHRC guidance for protecting research outputs and sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagining Canada’s Future (strategic priorities / knowledge mobilization)
rubrics_metrics.description: SSHRC mobilizes social sciences and humanities research and talent to address emerging societal challenges for Canada.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding opportunities and knowledge mobilization activities may align with SSHRC strategic priorities—applicants should consider how proposals address national challenges and impact when framing projects.
